_doc: DESIGN-LANGUAGE-1: one design language for every Ultrastable portfolio and every product that rolls up to it. Four layers, each allowed to vary only what the layer above permits. Consumed by foundation/design.py (python3 -m foundation design --check|--lint|--css|--tokens|--derive), tests/foundation/test_design.py, and the design-manager role (agents/roles/design-manager.md). Edit data here; never hand-edit a generated token file.

layers.core: Structure that never varies between portfolios or products: the --ds-* token contract, the 8 px spacing scale, the type scale ratios, tap size, contrast floors, focus ring, motion rules, the component set and the state rules. A product that needs to break one of these is a defect in the core, fixed in the core.
layers.portfolio: The family look of one organization: neutrals, accent seed, type pair, shape (radius flavor), density, voice. All products of the portfolio inherit it. The portfolio is the thing a stranger recognizes across products.
layers.product: One product's identity inside the family: an accent hue within the portfolio's hue range, a display face from the portfolio's allowed list, a density step, a mark. Everything else is inherited.
layers.experiment: A bounded variant of a product theme under test (doctrine/design-experiments.json). It may vary only what the product layer may vary, never the core.

ultrastable.voice: Confident, plain, practical, a little bold. Large serif headlines, wide margins, flat colour blocks, one orange action per screen.

ultrastable-site.role: public front door and marketing pages

ultrastable-cockpit.role: the owner's dashboard: dense, calm, scannable

tenants._doc: A system built on Ultrastable is a portfolio of its own. At bootstrap it picks ONE accent seed (a colour, or one the interview infers) and inherits everything else from the portfolio named here; `design --derive <hex>` makes the contrast-proven tokens, so a person never configures a design.
tenants.selection: automatic from the library (design --select); a person is never shown a font, colour or theme picker

surfaces_lint._doc: Surfaces checked by `design --lint`. `baseline` is shrink-only: findings listed there are known debt with a Q- item; a new finding fails the build.

research._doc: What the language is built from. Each entry is a practice adopted into the code, with where it lives. A source that stops paying (no finding adopted in 90 days) is replaced by the scout pass.

practices.source: Material 3 dynamic colour and Radix Colors step scales
practices.adopted_as: foundation/design.py derive_theme: one seed colour yields a full light and dark token set whose pairs are proven, instead of hand-picked hex

practices.adopted_as: design --tokens writes $value/$type tokens so any tool reads the same values

practices.source: WCAG 2.2 (1.4.3 text contrast, 1.4.11 non-text contrast, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.8 target size)
practices.adopted_as: contrast_pairs and invariants.tap_px, proven per theme in both modes

practices.source: Nielsen Norman Group usability heuristics (recognition over recall, minimalist design)
practices.adopted_as: one primary action per screen, secondary tools behind a disclosure

practices.source: GOV.UK, Atlassian, Shopify Polaris and GitHub Primer: core tokens plus themeable layers, contribution through the system
practices.adopted_as: layers, product_may_vary, product_may_not_vary, shrink-only lint baseline

practices.adopted_as: a second reviewer of a different model family on every surface change

library._doc: DESIGN-LIBRARY-1: a small, curated library of whole personalities, so every deployment looks like itself without anyone choosing a font or a colour. A personality is a bundle that was composed once and proven once: accent seed, neutral family, type pairing, shape, density. The system selects one automatically from the idea's own words (design --select) and a deployment's person is never asked. The library stays small on purpose: eight bundles give distinct looks without a menu; a ninth must differ from every existing one (design --check enforces pairwise distinctness) and earn its place by an experiment. Fonts are system stacks with a named first choice: no download, no layout shift, nothing to host.
library.selection: automatic: score each personality by the idea's words, break ties and spread deployments by a stable hash of the tenant id, and skip personalities a sibling deployment already uses (`taken`). With no signal the hash alone chooses. The person is never asked; the interview infers the words it already collects.
